prompt: Explain how to migrate an orders database safely. Include SQL and operational notes. Do not use tools.
answer:
A database migration should separate schema preparation from data conversion.

```sql
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN archived_at timestamptz;
CREATE INDEX orders_customer_idx ON orders(customer_id);
COMMIT;

SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS outstanding
FROM orders
WHERE archived_at IS NULL
GROUP BY customer_id
ORDER BY outstanding DESC;
```

Run the schema change against a disposable database first. Seed several customers with overlapping order histories so the aggregation exercises more than one group.

Deploy readers that accept the nullable timestamp before enabling writers. Existing records remain active until the background conversion assigns their archival time.

Use small batches for the conversion. Save a durable checkpoint after each transaction and resume from that checkpoint after a restart. Measure lock waits, replication delay, and query duration while the batches run.

A rollback should stop new writes to the column before older readers are restored. Keep the migration journal until the deployment has been stable across a full maintenance window.

Migration review complete.
